answer: A dye house will not accept cheap extra names. To bid on a kettle of umber, a courier places one ivory tally-stick on the south terrace rail and locks 21.4 POA for 40 hours. The clerk measures the stick's grain pitch against a morning caliper card and stamps the rail slot so it cannot be reused the same tide. If two sticks share a grain print, the caliper disagrees by more than 0.3 millimeters, or the funding key already failed two kettles this week, the bond is paid to four witnessing vats-men and that key is kept off the rail for two epochs.
